title: Getting a clarinet at 14; quadrille music at home dances
summary: Clarinet from his grandfather at 14, toy flutes and harmonica, and the quadrille dance music his father played at house parties.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: About how old were you? When I started? When you got your clarinet.
Oh, it was given to me by my grand-aad. I think I was 14 years old.
And you ever played around those little canon flutes, you know, like they have some of the kids played?
Oh yes, I played that and they had another thing they called a juice hop and I played a mouth hop, a French hop they used to call it. Harmonica something you called it. Yeah, harmonica, yeah.
So I wondered what music you first heard when you were young, if there was something in your home like your father, or would you hear parades or bands playing around the neighborhood?

Oh, my father. No, he always had an accordion. And during my childhood time, as far as I can remember, that when they would have these house parties, why they'd get him to play for us. So naturally I would go along with him too.
Was it sort of dance music?
Oh yeah, he played dance music, yeah. They had old tunes as a, let's see what they called them at that time. I can't think of the name of it.
Do you remember any of the quadrilles?
Yeah, that's what they were, quadrilles, yeah.
Did he play other things like more of the folk music and blues or anything of that kind?

No, during that time in my childhood there wasn't so much blues. It was mostly called ragtime. They didn't play that, it was all quadrilles. No. Because they had one guy who would be over there howling the dance and they'd go around the floor to take the beds down, you know, the great big rooms.
They'd have those dances right in their home then?
Yeah, right in the home, not in no dance hall, no right in the home.
